posts.title_en: Princess Bari's buff is bad?
posts.summary_en: Long discussion (16 comments) arguing Princess Bari's kit (DR + launch/knockback immunity for 'assault'-type cookies) doesn't solve the real problem, which is that Milk's ATK buff is positional and doesn't reach assault-type formations. Commenters note launch resistance is already solved by Pinot+Panda, and knockback resistance is separately gated (only ghost-type pets raise it). Consensus: Bari is not obviously a raid damage lever by herself; her value is speculative pending her 'soul damage' mechanic being measured.
mechanics: Knockback (밀치기) resistance is a separate stat from launch/lift (띄우기) resistance; Pinot/Panda only cover launch, not knockback. Only 'ghost'-type pets raise knockback resistance.
disagreements: Community split on whether Bari is worth building around for the raid: skeptics say her buff doesn't fix Milk's positional-buff problem; others hold out hope her damage-over-time ('soul') mechanic could be very strong once measured.

posts.title_en: But skill haste isn't good for every dealer
posts.summary_en: Argues multi-hit ('연타') skill users (named example: Dark Cacao/호두, and Cherry Cola/딸크) feel like skill amp gives ~500x value for them specifically, because their true cooldown is dominated by the multi-hit animation, not the nominal skill cooldown that haste reduces — e.g. Cherry Cola's stated 4s cooldown runs concurrently with a ~0.75s-interval, 5-hit punch combo, so haste barely shortens the real time between casts once the combo is already near-continuous. Conclusion (multiple commenters): haste has a much lower ceiling on multi-hit attackers than on single-cast attackers like Brightseeker, so skill amp is the better investment for that subset.

sugar_runes.why: Multi-hit cooldown is masked by the combo's own animation length, so haste has a low ceiling on multi-hit dealers.
Same multi-hit mechanic; 4s nominal cooldown but hits every ~0.75s during the combo, making the combo itself nearly continuous.

mechanics: Skill cooldown timers start counting down when the skill is CAST, so a long multi-hit animation (e.g. a 5-hit punch combo) already overlaps most of the nominal cooldown; extra haste on such a cookie yields far less real DPS than the same haste on a single-cast cookie like Brightseeker.
disagreements: Contradicts a blanket 'stack haste everywhere' reading of the existing gear/rune notes — this is a specific carve-out for multi-hit dealers (not Brightseeker), consistent with existing dashboard notes that Dark Choco already runs haste for a different reason (reapplying DEF shred), so check for conflation.

posts.title_en: The raid's structure feels really bizarre
posts.summary_en: A synthesis-level thread directly explaining WHY score variance is so extreme (30x-500x among similarly built accounts): Milk/Pomegranate/Macaron's buffs are all positional/conditional (must land on the correct cookie by ATK order or formation), rather than flat team-wide buffs. Multiple commenters agree this — not raw stat investment — is the actual source of the wide floor-to-peak spread: score measures 'how well the buff chain landed' as much as it measures gear/level investment.
rng: Explains the median-vs-peak gap directly: because all three key buffs (Milk, Pomegranate, Macaron) are conditional on ATK order/position rather than flat/team-wide, two accounts with identical investment can differ 30x-500x depending purely on how reliably the buff chain landed that run.
mechanics: Reconfirms Tea Knight's tSSR skill functions as a 'launch pad' stat check: whichever cookie unlocks the next tSSR redefines the raid meta and forces a full re-optimization ('발사대'), implying today's Cherry-deck ATK-order optimization is inherently temporary.

quotes.kr: 그게 지금 우석마치 버프가 전부 조건부라서 그래 아군 위치 상관없이 아군 전체로 버프 줬으면 저점고점 편차 안 심했을 텐데 우석마치 버퍼가 전부 조건부 범위다 보니까 얼마나 버프가 잘 들어갔냐고 점수가 나와서 그러는 거
quotes.en: It's because the Milk/Pomegranate/Macaron/Tea Knight buffs are all conditional. If they buffed the whole team regardless of position, the floor-to-peak spread wouldn't be this severe — since they're all conditional-range buffers, your score comes out as 'how well did the buff land.'

IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION: the same screenshot's '길드 랭킹' (guild ranking) panel shows totals of 4T791G / 4T574G / 4T371G — these are GUILD-WIDE AGGREGATE damage sums across ~30 members each, NOT a single player's run; do not read these as individual score records. In a reply, the author quantifies star investment: Brightseeker 7★→8★ alone gave only ~10% more damage over a ~340G(억?) baseline ('3400억' = 340G), while raising Milk's own star breakthrough had a noticeably bigger felt impact than the Brightseeker star-up.

mechanics: Star-up value is uneven across cookies: Brightseeker 7★→8★ measured ~10% over a ~340G baseline (smaller than the deck notes' earlier 4★→5★ jump), while Milk's own star breakthrough was felt to matter more, per the same player.
disagreements: Naming clarification only: guild-ranking totals in screenshots are guild-wide sums, not individual damage records — flagged to avoid the dataset (or a future reader) mistaking a 4T+ guild total for a 4T+ individual run.

quotes.kr: 브시커 7>8 자체로는 막 큰 체감 안됐고 우유 9성다는거 선택권으로 올리니까 체감 컸음 브시커 자체로는 3400억에서 한 10퍼정도 올린듯

quotes.kr: 고점은 메소 넣고 이속조절하는게 더 높을텐디 나는 세계선 찾을 자신이 없어서 걍 체리넣은상태로 어디까지 올라가나 해보는중

levers.lever: ATK-order discipline: keep every non-carry (fillers, backstops) strictly below all 6 named buffers' ATK, in-battle, not just in the lobby
levers.effect_claim: A single un-reset filler level (invisible unless checked mid-battle) silently caps the score at a fraction of what the build should do, regardless of runes/gear/power; fixing it alone took one player from stuck-below-400x to 400x immediately.
levers.numbers: Before/after: stuck <400x → 400x from one Scorpion-level reset (dc:74994). 6-drone/5-star Brightseeker is treated as a hard gate for ~500x (dc:74911, 'necessary').
levers.conditions: Cherry deck, ATK order Milk-Bright-(Macaron/Skating Queen)-...-TeaKnight-Cheesecake; must be checked in-battle because a pet (Octo Wasabi, +8%) can reorder ranks live.

levers.lever: Convert stat allocation from ATK% to skill amp on non-Milk cookies once the ATK order is locked
levers.effect_claim: Switching a team from an ATK%-heavy build to a skill-amp-heavy build raises the damage MULTIPLE even though it lowers the displayed team power, because skill amp scales buffer skills (Milk's ATK buff, Macaron's crit buff, Pomegranate's beam) rather than just raw hits.
levers.numbers: One account: 1.88G power / 500G damage (265x) on ATK%. Author's own skill-amp hypothetical: ~1.3G power / ~600G (~460x). A commenter's estimate for the same account fixing ATK order too: ~700G (~372x on the higher power, or higher still on the lower).
levers.conditions: Applies to cookies other than Milk (who should stay all-ATK% because her buff scales off her own ATK). Rebuild cost (rerolling sugar runes) is real; disputed whether already-ATK%-invested accounts should pay it.
disagreements: Author of dc:70064 argues the rune-reroll cost may not be worth it for someone already deep into ATK%; 캔디애플 and another commenter argue skill amp is the objectively higher ceiling and worth switching to, especially for anyone still building.

levers.lever: Skill haste has a low ceiling on multi-hit ('연타') skill users; skill amp is the better investment for those specific cookies
levers.effect_claim: Multi-hit dealers' true attack rate is bottlenecked by their combo animation length, not the nominal cooldown haste reduces, so haste yields little extra DPS on them once the combo is already near-continuous; skill amp is described as feeling like '500x' for those cookies.
levers.numbers: Example given: a 4s nominal cooldown skill that fires 5 hits at ~0.75s intervals during its own combo (dc:68867, qualitative, no isolated A/B number).
levers.conditions: Applies to multi-hit dealers (examples named: Dark Cacao/호두, Cherry Cola/딸크), NOT to single-cast cookies like Brightseeker, where the existing haste-breakpoint model (haste to ~40 total) still holds.
disagreements: Existing dashboard mechanics.json documents Dark Choco running haste for a different reason (reapplying DEF-shred faster); this lever's claim about multi-hit dealers generally needs reconciling with that per-cookie exception rather than read as a blanket rule.

levers.lever: Milk's own star-breakthrough investment matters more than expected relative to Brightseeker's late stars
levers.effect_claim: One player felt Brightseeker's 7★→8★ upgrade alone gave only a modest gain, while raising Milk's own star-choice option had a noticeably bigger felt impact on the same run.
levers.numbers: Brightseeker 7★→8★: ~10% over a ~340G baseline (single data point).
levers.conditions: Both cookies were otherwise maxed (Lv.100, near-complete runes) on the same 915M-power account.

levers.lever: Pet star investment (Candy Shade Pouch, and by extension other raid pets) has sharply diminishing returns past 10-15 stars
levers.effect_claim: Community consensus is that pulling a raid pet to 20 stars is not worth it; 10 (or at most 15) stars already captures most of the value.
levers.numbers: Qualitative only ('효율 ㅅㅌㅊ' = decent efficiency) at 10★; no isolated damage delta given.
levers.conditions: Specific to Candy Shade Pouch in the thread, but framed as general pet-investment advice.

levers.lever: Survival past the 17s wipe is gated by a specific 3-pet HP/lift-resistance combo, not by HP/DR runes alone
levers.effect_claim: Candy Shade Pouch's 30% lift resistance alone (no Pinot) is insufficient; the emerging consensus 'meta' pairs Choco King Bell (raw HP) + Ice Bird + Candy Shade Pouch together, consistent with the dashboard's existing 9M HP / 45% DR survival threshold finding.
levers.numbers: Existing dashboard figures reconfirmed: ~9M HP + 45% DR per surviving cookie (dc:74801, dc:69856); this batch adds the 3-pet combo framing (dc:72559) and the 'pouch alone isn't enough' negative result (dc:73742).
levers.conditions: Raid-specific; Pinot's lift resistance must stack with, not be replaced by, the pouch's.

levers.lever: Move-speed-tuned formation (Melon Soda-style) has a materially higher damage ceiling than the Cherry-forced-line formation, at equal power
levers.effect_claim: Multiple top posters state directly that the move-speed-tuned deck's peak is meaningfully higher than Cherry's, but describe the tuning itself as too fragile/risky to reliably execute, so they stay on Cherry despite knowing it caps their ceiling lower.
levers.numbers: No new isolated number beyond the existing dashboard figures (Melon Soda ceiling ≈1T at 1.6G/625x vs Cherry's higher documented peaks); this batch reconfirms the qualitative ranking from players actively choosing not to attempt it.
levers.conditions: Per-account, per-device move-speed tuning to hundredths; previously documented as failing ~1 in 4 runs even when tuned.

levers.lever: The 17s 'wipe' is gradual (starting ~19s remaining), not an instant simultaneous kill at 17s
levers.effect_claim: Cookies die one or two at a time starting around 19s remaining rather than all at once at 17s, meaning survival tuning is a continuum (each extra ~1-2s of an individual cookie's life adds some damage) rather than a single pass/fail threshold.
levers.conditions: Team was mostly Lv.1 fillers except the 6 named carries.

levers.lever: Score variance (30x-500x among similarly built accounts) is structurally explained by the CONDITIONAL/positional nature of the Milk/Pomegranate/Macaron/Tea Knight buffs, not primarily by raw stat gaps
levers.effect_claim: Because these key buffs only land on the correct cookie by ATK order or formation rather than buffing the whole team unconditionally, score measures 'how well the buff chain landed this run' as much as it measures investment — this is offered by the community itself as the root explanation for why a 550G median vs a 1T+ peak can come from the same account.
levers.numbers: Qualitative, but consistent with observed spreads elsewhere in the dataset (e.g. dc:71066's 4-5G floor vs 14.4G peak on one account).
levers.conditions: General to the raid's buff design, not specific to one deck.

levers.lever: Reverse-engineered exchange rate: ATK% and skill amp are NOT 1:1; roughly 1% ATK% ≈ 0.617% skill amp in damage terms
levers.effect_claim: A dedicated stat-testing post derived this conversion ratio by isolating ATK%-only vs skill-amp-only sugar rune sets against a fixed stage boss and reverse-solving the damage formula.
levers.numbers: 1% ATK increase = 0.617% skill amp increase, in terms of equivalent damage output (nv:24362).
levers.conditions: Derived on 2026-08-23 against a Stage boss (168-30), BEFORE the 8/27 patch that removed skill amp's effect on stat-reduction debuffs and DR buffs — likely stale for the current raid meta and not raid-specific; flagged as a historical baseline only, not a current-patch number.
disagreements: Superseded in spirit by the current forum consensus (dashboard's existing decks.json/runes.json) that skill amp should be prioritized on nearly every cookie except Milk — this pre-nerf 0.617 ratio undersells skill amp's current relative value if taken literally today.

levers.lever: Macaron's own skill amp allegedly converts to team crit rate at roughly 1:1.1
levers.effect_claim: 1% skill amp invested on Macaron raises allies' crit rate by about 1.1%, offered as the justification for keeping skill amp on her rather than switching to ATK% even once a team can survive to Lv.1-filler-viable states.
levers.numbers: 1% skill amp → +1.1% ally crit rate (single-poster claim).
levers.conditions: Unverified formula; no second independent source found in this batch or the existing dataset.
disagreements: No counter-source, but also no corroborating source beyond agreement replies in the same thread; treat as an open, unverified quantitative claim worth checking against datamined formulas.

levers.lever: Lab (연구소) HP research prioritized over ATK/DEF research raises 30s-slam survival independent of sugar runes/gear
levers.effect_claim: A player who focused lab HP research reports nearly the whole team surviving the 30s slam as a result, with a commenter agreeing HP research should be prioritized ahead of ATK research.
levers.numbers: Qualitative only ('거의 다 생존함' = almost everyone survives).
levers.conditions: Independent, additive lever on top of gear/rune HP and DR investment; not previously logged in the dashboard's mechanics/gear notes as a distinct account-wide lever.
